newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity Magellan cut bonds to nil in February.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Magellan cut bonds to nil in February.

text.p: Fidelity Investments's flagship Magellan Fund cut its holdings in bonds to nil at the end of February from 0.8 percent of assets at the end of January, according to the monthly Fidelity Mutual Fund Guide.
Magellan also cut its holdings in cash to 4.5 percent of assets at the end of February, the most recent month for which figures are available, from 5.7 percent a month earlier.
The fund raised its stock holdings to 95.5 percent of assets from 93.5 percent, the guide said.
Magellan cut its holdings in technology stocks to 13.8 percent of assets from 14.6 percent, cut energy shares to 13.1 percent from 14.6 percent, and raised finance to 10.5 percent from 9.6 percent.
Assets in durables slipped to 8.8 percent from 8.9 percent, industrial machinery and equipment rose to 7.9 percent from 7.7 percent, and healthcare shares rose to 7.3 percent from 6.3 percent.
Magellan added Merck and Co Inc, Exxon Corp and American International Group Inc to its top 10 holdings at the end of February.
The fund cut International Business Machines Corp, Royal Dutch Petroleum Co and Cisco Systems Inc from its top 10 holdings, Fidelity said.
Remaining among the top 10 were General Electric Co, Intel Corp, Philip Morris Cos Inc, CSX Corp, Chrysler Corp, Citicorp and Schlumberger Ltd.
Total assets in the fund, the largest in the U.S., fell to $51.4 billion at the end of March from $53.8 billion at the end of February, Fidelity said.
Investments in foreign securities slipped to 9.9 percent of assets at the end of February from 10.4 percent at the end of January.
The fund recorded a negative return of 0.56 percent for the first three months 1997, versus a gain of 2.68 percent for the S&P 500 over that period, the guide said.

Since he took over Magellan in June, fund manager Robert Stansky has gradually shifted the fund into stocks and out of its massive investment in bonds, which hurt the fund's returns over the past year when the stock market recorded strong gains.
